research_rationale:
EO 6874 (October 16, 1934, Franklin D. Roosevelt), read in full. Text and identity: read in full in the registered American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-28: the APP page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/(MIRROR_)DOCUMENTS.jsonl has a heading naming this order number, a date and subject agreeing with the held text, and a text_sha256 equal to the held file's. Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy.  It is not a closing order (the type label closing_mourning is wrong; the WPA 1944 list, 1935 CSR 28, and the APP title agree): under the Civil Service Act of January 16, 1883 it amends paragraph 6 of subdivision VII of schedule A of the civil-service rules 'to read as follows': '6. Temporary clerks, carriers, and laborers required for part-time or intermittent work in the Postal Service in connection with the present holiday or seasonal business from this date to February 1, 1935.' Decision on its own terms. The order's one command is the rewrite of paragraph 6; under the strike-and-insert ruling the rewritten paragraph is the operative clause and continues, amended, until something ends it. Two candidate ends exist in held evidence. (a) The inserted text's own period: the paragraph excepts positions only 'from this date to February 1, 1935'. That period is part of the exception's definition, so after February 1, 1935 the paragraph excepted no position; the text itself is the evidence that its operation ended, and nothing held extended it (the WPA 1944 list shows no amendment of subdivision VII paragraph 6 between October 16, 1934 and October 19, 1935). (b) EO 7209 (October 19, 1935; held government-printed text, added here as SUPPLEMENT:EO7209) amends paragraph 6 'to read as follows' with a new period to February 1, 1936; its words show it replaced the paragraph's text, but by then the 1934 exception had already stopped operating. Conclusion: the clause terminated by its own terms on 1935-02-01, read inclusively (exclusive alternative: it stopped when that day began, so January 31, 1935 was its last day); EO 7209's replacement of the spent text on 1935-10-19 is recorded as a later event, not as the end. Under the evidence-decides ruling EO 7209 is not a default end, and here the earlier own-terms end is evidenced. Savings: appointments made under the exception during its period are accrued; they do not keep the exception operative. Earlier versions of paragraph 6 (EO 5731, 1931; EO 5930, 1932; EO 6352, 1933) precede this order and do not affect its end.
